plan: This auction mechanism functions as a second-price auction: the winner pays the second-highest bid, regardless of the ascending clock mechanics. In such formats, bidding one's true value is the dominant strategy - it maximizes expected profit without risk of overpaying, since you only pay the second-highest bid if you win. Bidding above value risks losing money if you win at a price above your value; bidding below value risks losing profitable opportunities. Therefore, I will bid exactly my true value of $36.

This auction structure is equivalent to a second-price sealed-bid auction: the winner pays the second-highest bid, and my exit point is determined by my own sealed bid. Bidding my true value ($8) is a dominant strategy here - if I bid higher, I risk winning and overpaying relative to my value; if I bid lower, I risk losing auctions I could have profitably won. Truthful bidding maximizes expected profit regardless of others' strategies.

Since the winner pays the second-highest sealed bid (equivalent to a second-price auction), the dominant strategy is to bid my true value. Bidding exactly my value ensures I win whenever my value exceeds others' bids, paying only the second-highest bid, which guarantees non-negative profit and maximizes expected profit. There's no incentive to shade or inflate my bid.
